# Deep sequence forecaster (Task 4, optional)

**SIMULATED DATA.** Generated by `ml/deep_forecast.py` (`--report-only` rebuilds this file).

**Model.** GRU (1×64) over the last 60 minutes of the Model 3 feature set (63 features), linear head, L1 loss, Adam (lr 0.001), batch 512, early stopping on validation MAE (patience 4, at most 30 epochs), seed 42. Imputation and scaling fitted on training minutes only. No architecture search.

**Split.** whole UTC days: 5 train / 1 validation / 1 test (later partial data left out); test rows identical to the ablation's (checked at runtime).

| Target | h | GRU skill | GRU MAE | XGBoost (Model 3) skill | XGBoost MAE | Epochs (best) | n test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| noise_dba | 30 | **+0.518** | 3.89 | +0.760 | 1.94 | 23 (19) | 9,720 |
| noise_dba | 60 | **+0.676** | 2.63 | +0.787 | 1.73 | 21 (17) | 9,510 |

Training time: 4.7 min (cap 45 min).

## Conclusion

GRU (1×64) over the last 60 minutes of the Model 3 feature set, same split and test rows (noise_dba_h30: GRU skill +0.518 (MAE 3.89) against XGBoost on the same features +0.760 (MAE 1.94); noise_dba_h60: GRU skill +0.676 (MAE 2.63) against XGBoost on the same features +0.787 (MAE 1.73)). Deep sequence models offered no advantage over gradient boosting on this dataset, likely because the engineered lag features already capture the temporal structure. Details: `results_deep_forecast.md`.

**Scope of the claim.** This is one modest configuration with no architecture search, as the brief required. The validation error plateaued for many epochs and then dropped late, so the GRU may be under-trained, and a larger search might narrow the gap. The finding is that *a modest sequence model adds nothing here*, not that sequence models cannot work. No confidence interval is reported (one test day); the gap is large relative to the ablation's intervals, but that is an observation, not a test.
